message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Compute Engine instance in Google Cloud that is configured with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU (if it is available in your region) and boots from the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image.  
If the RTX A6000 is not yet offered in your chosen zone, the example will still work with the next‑best GPU (e.g., NVIDIA Tesla A100) – just change the `type` field accordingly.

> **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the term “EC2”; that is AWS terminology.  
> * The RTX A6000 is not currently listed as a supported GPU type in the Compute Engine API. If you try to use it, you’ll receive an error.  
> * Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ZONE`, and `YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME` with your own values.  
> * You must have the Compute Engine API enabled, billing enabled, and the `gcloud` CLI authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).

---

## 1. gcloud CLI Command

```bash
gcloud compute instances create YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME \
  --zone=YOUR_ZONE \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | The Compute Engine zone where the instance will live. |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/memory configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs and 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds a GPU. Replace `nvidia-tesla-a6000` with `nvidia-tesla-a100` if the former is unavailable. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Terminates the instance during maintenance events (useful for GPU workloads). |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Automatically restarts the instance if it crashes. |

---

## 2. REST API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s the exact JSON payload you would POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  }
}
```

### How to send it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/instances"
```

> Replace `@instance.json` with the path to a file containing the JSON above.

---

## 3. Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Enable Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`) |
| ✅ | Enable Cloud Billing for your project |
| ✅ | Verify GPU availability in your zone (`gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone=YOUR_ZONE`) |
| ✅ | Authenticate `gcloud` (`gcloud auth login`) |
| ✅ | Run the CLI command or POST the JSON |

---

### If RTX A6000 is Unavailable

If you run into an error like:

```
ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) The requested accelerator type nvidia-tesla-a6000 is not available in zone YOUR_ZONE.
```

Replace the accelerator type with a supported one, e.g.:

```bash
--accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1
```

or check the full list:

```bash
gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone=YOUR_ZONE
```

---

That’s all you need! Once the instance is up, you can SSH into it, install the NVIDIA drivers, and start your GPU workloads. Happy computing!
